title: being the argument of a trusted binding buys a callback body no ambient authority
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Host Globals' (Locked): "Host-sensitive operations such as clock and random access MUST still use capabilities." The host-global check never consults the enclosing call, so the acceptance granted by 09-foreign-calls/a-callback-registered-through-a-trusted-binding-is-accepted adds no opt-out that ordinary code could claim — the only thing that rule reads is a JSDoc `@throws` tag on a FOREIGN declaration, which authored `.sm` cannot write about itself. The third of the three guards, and the one that matters most: it is the ambient-authority direction.
